title: Which worshipper God accepts
source_text: Καὶ σὺ γὰρ σκόπησον παρὰ σαυτῷ, ποῖον παραδέξεται μᾶλλον ἦθος ὁ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸς, καὶ δυνάμενος ὅσα ἄλλος οὐδεὶς πρὸς πάντα καὶ πρὸς εὐεργεσίαν ἀνθρώπων εἴτε περὶ ψυχὴν εἴτε περὶ σῶμα εἴτε περὶ τὰ ἐκτὸς, πότερον τὸν αὐτῷ περὶ πάντων ἀνακείμενον ἢ τὸν περιεργαζόμενον δαιμόνων ὀνόματα καὶ δυνάμεις καὶ πράξεις καὶ ἐπῳδὰς καὶ βοτάνας οἰκείας δαίμοσι καὶ λίθους καὶ τὰς ἐν αὐτοῖς γλυφὰς, καταλλήλους ταῖς παραδιδομέναις εἴτε συμβολικαῖς εἴτε ὅπως ποτὲ μορφαῖς δαιμόνων. ἀλλὰ δῆλον τῷ καὶ ἐπ᾿ ὀλίγον παρακολουθεῖν δυναμένῳ ὅτι τὸ ἄπλαστον μὲν καὶ ἀπερίεργον ἦθος διὰ τοῦτο θεῷ τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσιν ἀνακείμενον ἀποδεκτὸν ἔσται θεῷ καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς ἐκείνῳ οἰκειουμένοις· τὸ δὲ δι᾿ ὑγείαν σώματος καὶ φιλοσωματίαν καὶ τὴν ἐν μέσοις πράγμασιν εὐτυχίαν περιεργαζόμενον δαιμόνων ὀνόματα καὶ ζητοῦν. πῶς κηλήσει τισὶν ἐπῳδαῖς τοὺς δαίμονας, ὡς μοχθηρὸν καὶ ἀσεβὲς καὶ δαιμονικὸν μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρωπικὸν καταλείψει ὁ θεὸς οἷς εἵλετο ὁ τὰ τοιάδε λέγων δαίμοσι, διασπαραχθησόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν ὑφ᾿ ἑκάστου ὑποβαλλομένων λογισμῶν ἢ καὶ ἄλλων κακῶν. εἰκὸς γὰρ αὐτοὺς ἅτε φαύλους ὄντας καὶ, ὡς Κέλσος ὡμολόγησε, προσηλωμένους αἵματι καὶ κνίσσῃ καὶ μελῳδίαις καὶ ἄλλοις τισὶ τοιούτοις μηδὲ πρὸς τοὺς ταῦτα αὐτοῖς χαριζομένους πίστιν τηρεῖν καὶ οἱονεὶ δεξιάς. ἄλλων γὰρ αὐτοὺς καλούντων κατὰ τῶν θεραπευσάντων καὶ πλείονος αἵματος καὶ κνίσσης καὶ ἧς δέονται θεραπείας ὠνουμένων αὐτῶν τὴν δουλείαν, ἐπιβουλεύσαιεν ἂν τῷ χθὲς αὐτοὺς θεραπεύσαντι καὶ τῆς φίλης αὐτοῖς θοίνης μεταδιδόντι.
pass_a_gloss: Consider (σκοπέω) yourself which character (ἦθος) the God over all will more accept (παραδέχομαι), being able for as much as no other for all things and for the benefiting (εὐεργεσία) of men, whether about soul or body or outward things (τὰ ἐκτός): whether the one devoted (ἀνάκειμαι) to Him about all things, or the one meddling with / busying himself with (περιεργάζομαι) names of demons and powers (δυνάμεις) and actions (πράξεις) and incantations (ἐπῳδαί) and herbs (βοτάναι) proper (οἰκεῖαι) to demons and stones (λίθοι) and the carvings (γλυφαί) in them, corresponding (κατάλληλοι) to the handed-down (παραδίδωμι) forms (μορφαί) of demons, whether symbolic (συμβολικαί) or however. But it is clear to one able even a little to follow (παρακολουθέω) that the unfeigned (ἄπλαστον) and unmeddling (ἀπερίεργον) character, for this reason devoted to the God over all, will be acceptable (ἀποδεκτόν) to God and to all made kin (οἰκειόομαι) to Him; but the one that for bodily health (ὑγεία) and love of the body (φιλοσωματία) and good fortune (εὐτυχία) in middle matters (μέσα πράγματα) busies itself with names of demons and seeks how it will charm (κηλέω) the demons with certain incantations, as wicked (μοχθηρόν) and impious (ἀσεβές) and demonic (δαιμονικόν) rather than human (ἀνθρωπικόν), God will leave (καταλείπω) to those whom he chose (αἱρέομαι), the one saying such things to demons, to be torn apart (διασπαράσσω) by the thoughts (λογισμοί) suggested (ὑποβάλλω) by each or also by other evils. For it is likely that they, being base (φαῦλοι) and, as Celsus admitted (ὁμολογέω), nailed to blood and savour and melodies and other such things, do not keep faith (πίστις) and as it were right hands / pledges (δεξιαί) even toward those gratifying (χαρίζομαι) them with these things. For when others call them against those who served them, and buy (ὠνέομαι) their servitude (δουλεία) with more blood and savour and the service they need, they would plot against (ἐπιβουλεύω) the one who yesterday (χθές) served them and shared (μεταδίδωμι) the feast (θοίνη) dear to them.
pass_b_english: Consider for yourself too: which character will the God over all more readily accept, He who has power as no one else has, for all things and for doing good to men, whether in soul or in body or in outward things? Will it be the one devoted to Him in all things, or the one who busies himself with the names of demons, their powers and workings, with spells and herbs suited to demons, with stones and the carvings on them, made to match the forms of demons that have been handed down, whether symbolic or of some other kind?

It is clear to anyone who can follow the argument even a little that the character free of pretence and free of curious arts, and for that very reason devoted to the God over all, will be acceptable to God and to all who are His own. But the character that, for the sake of bodily health, love of the body and good fortune in things that are neither good nor bad, busies itself with the names of demons and seeks how it may charm the demons with certain spells, God will leave, as wicked, impious and more demonic than human, to the demons chosen by the man who addresses such words to them, to be torn apart by the thoughts each of them suggests, or by other evils as well.

For it is likely that, being base, and, as Celsus admitted, nailed to blood and the smoke of sacrifice and to songs and other such things, they do not keep faith, or their pledges, so to speak, even toward those who gratify them with these things. For when others call on them against those who have served them, and buy their service with more blood and smoke of sacrifice and the worship they crave, they would plot against the man who served them yesterday and gave them a share of the feast they love.

choices.choice: τὸν αὐτῷ ... ἀνακείμενον and τὸν περιεργαζόμενον are masculine though ἦθος is neuter (sense construction: the person of that character). ἀπερίεργον and περιεργάζομαι carry the sense of meddling in curious or magical arts (compare τὰ περίεργα in Acts 19:19); not cited, since no verse is being quoted. ἐν μέσοις πράγμασιν: the Stoic ‘middle things’ or things indifferent, rendered ‘things that are neither good nor bad’. Doubtful construction: οἷς εἵλετο ὁ τὰ τοιάδε λέγων δαίμοσι can mean ‘to those whom he chose, he who speaks such things to demons’ (δαίμοσι with λέγων) or ‘to the demons whom the man who says such things chose’ (δαίμοσι attracted into the relative); the English ‘to the demons chosen by the man who addresses such words to them’ covers both readings with one mention of the demons (reviewer’s revision of the draft’s doubled ‘to demons’). Koetschau’s stop after ζητοῦν is read as a pause. No Scripture is quoted.
Καὶ σὺ γὰρ σκόπησον: restored 'too' ('Consider for yourself too')
δυνάμενος ὅσα ἄλλος οὐδείς ... πρὸς εὐεργεσίαν smoothed: 'has power as no one else has ... for doing good to men, whether in soul or in body'
οἷς εἵλετο ὁ τὰ τοιάδε λέγων δαίμοσι: removed doubled 'to demons'; 'to the demons chosen by the man who addresses such words to them'
καταλείψει 'abandon' to 'leave' (closer, and keeps the 'leave to' construction)

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.
